title: The story of Paris's 'cursed' island
subhead: On October 17, Le Large will open its doors – a small miracle given the many projects that have fallen through after Renault left Seguin Island, just west of Paris, in 1992. But the story is not over: The center of the island remains conspicuously empty.

Trump administration is trying to reshape election rules to its advantage ahead of midterm elections
subhead: The Supreme Court prevented Republicans on Friday from redrawing Missouri's electoral map to their benefit, but the party has managed to reshape districts in many other states. Meanwhile, the White House sought to purge voter rolls and limit mail-in voting.

title: India's Cockroach Party denounces crumbling schools: 'Children are treated worse than animals'
subhead: Founded just a few months ago, the Cockroach Janta Party, a Gen Z-led movement, has visited several schools and conducted an audit to expose the extent of their dilapidation and unsanitary conditions. Authorities have tried everything in their power to prevent the group from carrying out these inspections.

title: 'Prize-contending author Orélien's AI controversy challenges the literary world's postcard image of the solitary writer'
subhead: If artificial intelligence can find its way into a quality book, as it allegedly has in 'C'était Ça Ou Mourir' by the Canadian-Haitian novelist, currently topping sales charts and in contention for prizes, what does that mean for literature? We probably need to accept it, writes Le Monde's culture columnist Michel Guerrin.

title: Why France's Senate is increasingly unrepresentative
subhead: Roughly half of the 348 seats will be renewed on Sunday. But the current electoral map, based on 1999 census data, favors Paris and rural areas, to the detriment of regions whose populations have grown faster.

How Paris, New York and Tokyo are all moving away from car-centric urban planning
subhead: In a study presented on September 9, the Paris Urban Planning Workshop analyzed how residents in seven major cities have been getting around over the past 20 years. The profound transformation of public space has given rise to new practices: residents walk, cycle and take public transport more.

title: Half of its members are being renewed today. But what does the French Senate really do?
subhead: While it is rarely in the media spotlight, the Sénat is an essential cog in the country's democratic system. Local elected officials are voting to renew just over half of the seats this Sunday.

title: Leo XIV, a calm and unifying pope, draws huge crowds in Paris open-air mass
subhead: According to the Vatican, 800,000 people attended the event. In front of several presidential candidates, devout Catholics and the simply curious, the pope spoke in his homily about "the thirst for transcendence." He then left for Lourdes, the next stop on his journey.
